def choose_move(observation):
    agent = observation.get('agent', {})
    position = agent.get('position', (0, 0))
    resources = observation.get('resources', [])
    enemies = observation.get('enemies', [])
    territory = observation.get('territory', {})
    border = territory.get('border', [])

    # Combine all potential targets and prioritize:
    # Priority: resources, then enemies, then borders.
    targets = resources + enemies + border

    if targets:
        # Find the closest target
        target = min(targets, key=lambda t: abs(t[0] - position[0]) + abs(t[1] - position[1]))
        dx = target[0] - position[0]
        dy = target[1] - position[1]
        # Normalize to -1, 0, or 1
        dx = (dx > 0) - (dx < 0)
        dy = (dy > 0) - (dy < 0)
        return [dx, dy]
    else:
        # Default move when no targets are present
        # Use a simple pattern to move around
        # For robustness against opponents, prefer to move towards the origin
        dx = -1 if position[0] > 0 else (1 if position[0] < 0 else 0)
        dy = -1 if position[1] > 0 else (1 if position[1] < 0 else 0)
        return [dx, dy]
